docs.purpose: A dashboard an advertiser logs into to see how their own sponsored placements performed — how many times their offer was shown and how many times someone clicked it. It shows only their own numbers and no one else's, enforced by the database rather than by the page. This is the first screen in the estate handed to someone who is not an internal admin, which is why it is scoped by the advertiser's own identity instead of the admin flag.

checks.why: The one check this surface cannot ship without: an advertiser must never see another advertiser's numbers, and the proof is the Class-D policy asserted against pg_policies, not a WHERE clause in the route. It gates the render because a cross-tenant leak is not a post-render finding.
A tile that cannot compute renders "unavailable" in place; a blank tile on a page an external party reads is indistinguishable from "you had zero impressions".
The plausible-zero trap, and here it is commercial: "no impressions yet" and "the meter is not wired" must be visibly different to someone who paid.

R-23: an active in-flight offer with zero usage_events rows means the SLOT render path is not writing its impression — the dead-meter defect, and this is the page where an advertiser would notice it first.

The projection crosses a trust boundary to an external party; it must be an explicit pick-by-name whitelist that set-equals the contract, never a row spread that could carry user_id or session_id out of usage_events.
usage_events rows carry user_id OR session_id (the CHECK makes it exactly one); neither may be projected to an advertiser at any aggregation that could re-identify a viewer.
Every tile carries an accessible label; this is the one surface in the set whose audience is not an internal operator.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE (user_id IS NULL) = (session_id IS NULL)
invariants.why: Spec 126 §7's chk_usage_events_principal makes the principal exactly one of user_id / session_id; a row that is ambiguous about who it belongs to cannot be attributed, and an impression count built on it is unbillable.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE event NOT IN ('property_view','pdf_send','offer_impression','offer_click','export','parcel_id_translated')
invariants.why: The event vocabulary is closed; an unknown event would be silently excluded from every tile, which is how a count quietly under-reports.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT subject_key, count(*) FILTER (WHERE event='offer_click') AS c, count(*) FILTER (WHERE event='offer_impression') AS i FROM usage_events WHERE subject_kind='offer_id' GROUP BY 1) x WHERE x.c > x.i
invariants.why: More clicks than impressions is physically impossible and is the clearest single signal that the impression write is dropping rows — the cross-field invariant no per-field check would catch.

plausibility.sql: SELECT subject_key, count(*) FILTER (WHERE event='offer_click')::numeric / NULLIF(count(*) FILTER (WHERE event='offer_impression'),0) AS ctr FROM usage_events WHERE subject_kind='offer_id' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ctr DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
plausibility.why: A click-through rate is a bounded, domain-plausible quantity; a CTR at or near 1.0 is not a great advertiser, it is a double-counted click or a missing impression, and a number nobody looked at would bill on it.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM offers o WHERE o.active AND o.flight_start <= now() AND (o.flight_end IS NULL OR o.flight_end >= now()) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM usage_events u WHERE u.subject_kind='offer_id' AND u.subject_key = o.offer_id::text AND u.event='offer_impression')
plausibility.why: An in-flight offer with zero impressions is either a targeting miss or a dead meter, and only a human looking at the number can tell which.

limitations.what: guards.session cannot express this surface's principal.
limitations.measured: The closed set is anon | authenticated | entitled | admin (surface.schema.json guards.session.answer). The advertiser is a ROLE (Spec 126 §6.2 R-10), explicitly not an entitlement (R-09 draws that line for agent) and explicitly not is_admin-gated (Spec 126 §2.2 group D). The field is UNRESEARCHED until the vocabulary is ruled.

limitations.what: The DASHBOARD required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates tiles[] each with its own contract_ref and degrade_independently, plus refresh.poll_ms and per-tile states[], and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.

limitations.what: Nothing writes the rows this dashboard counts.
limitations.measured: Spec 126 §7 states there is no working meter to extend, and SponsorSlot.tsx returns null on both branches, so offer_impression has no producer today. The page would render a truthful zero, which is why advmetrics_ledger_row_present and advmetrics_impressions_per_active_offer both exist.

notes: Report §1.1 row 15: reads usage_events filtered to `event IN (offer_impression, offer_click)` AND the viewer's own advertiser_id; RLS-scoped, not is_admin-gated. §4.2 classifies this as the new RLS class D (owner-scoped by a key that is not auth.uid()). VERIFIED: no CREATE TABLE for usage_events in migrations/. No admin-side defect named for this row. DESIGNED, NOT MEASURED. THE ONE ROW WHOSE GUARD CANNOT BE STATED: guards.session is UNRESEARCHED because the closed vocabulary (anon | authenticated | entitled | admin) has no `advertiser` value, and Spec 126 draws the line deliberately — agent IS an entitlement (R-09), advertiser IS a role (R-10) — so "entitled" would contradict the ruling and "admin" contradicts the report. Also note the route is NOT under /admin/, so classifyRoute would return "authenticated" for it, which is the second half of the same gap.
